title: Mlai entry systemdesign batch vs online inference
topic: Mlai entry systemdesign batch vs online inference
question: Would you serve predictions with batch inference, precomputed ahead of time, or online inference, computed at request time, and what factors drive that choice?
idealAnswer:
Batch inference precomputes predictions on a schedule and stores them for lookup, it's simpler and cheaper but predictions can be stale by the time they're used

Online inference computes a prediction at request time using the freshest available features, needed when predictions must reflect very recent behavior, e.g. what the customer just viewed this session

Batch works well when the input space is small or enumerable, e.g. one prediction per user per day, and latency requirements are loose

Online inference requires more infrastructure: a low-latency serving endpoint, feature values available in real time, and tighter operational reliability requirements

A reasonable answer for this specific example leans toward batch if personalization doesn't need to react within the same session, or a hybrid approach if it does
